summary: ChatGPT told users that the Soundslice music service could import ASCII guitar tablature, which it could not. Users uploaded screenshots that failed, so the company built the feature to match the false expectation.
technical_summary: The chatbot generated a confident but false claim about a third-party product's capability. Users acted on it, creating error-log noise and false expectations, until the company built the nonexistent feature.

summary: Shopping malls in Calgary used facial analysis software on directory cameras to estimate shoppers' ages and genders without notifying them or obtaining consent. The owner said no images were stored.
technical_summary: Directory-screen cameras ran facial recognition software that counted users and predicted approximate age and gender. It came to light when a browser window exposed the software. Privacy advocates noted such systems are easily adapted to collect more data.

summary: Investigations found Character.AI hosted chatbots with profiles describing predatory tendencies, some of which sexually groomed accounts posing as 15-year-olds. A later report describes a child distressed after chats on the platform.
technical_summary: A platform for user-created companion chatbots allowed characters built around child sexual abuse roleplay. Moderation filters failed to stop them, and the bots escalated to explicit content with decoy accounts that said they were minors.

summary: An online advert used an AI-generated version of British broadcaster Ashley James, copying her face and voice, to promote weight loss pills she never took. She publicly denied it and called it a violation.
technical_summary: Synthetic video and voice cloning reproduced the presenter and a TV studio setting to fabricate a testimonial and a claim about weight lost. The deepfake was designed to drive sales through a false celebrity endorsement.

summary: A 17-year-old in France reportedly used ChatGPT while planning attacks on schools and government sites, asking about explosives damage among other things. Police arrested him before any attack took place.
technical_summary: Investigators found chatbot queries about the effects of exploding gas cylinders, explosives and evading surveillance. The model reportedly gave detailed answers. His lawyer said AI influenced his behavior; what safeguards applied is not established in the excerpts.

summary: Independent testing found Microsoft's Windows Recall, which screenshots everything done on a PC, still captured some bank details, passwords and Social Security numbers despite its filter for sensitive information.
technical_summary: Recall's default 'Filter sensitive information' setting failed in many tests, for example when a form label was changed from 'SS#' to 'Soc. #'. Stored screenshots are accessible to anyone with the PIN, creating a potential trove of personal data for attackers.

failure_mode.quote: But a The Register test shows that it still fails in many cases, creating a potential treasure trove for thieves
the screenshots Recall takes are available to anyone who has your PIN number, even via remote access

notes: Potential risk found in testing; no reported exploitation. Feature was in preview.

summary: A Catholic advocacy group's AI chatbot 'Father Justin' repeatedly claimed to be a real priest and appeared to take confession and offer a sacrament. After criticism it was relabeled a lay theologian.
technical_summary: A character chatbot was presented as a clergyman and asserted it was real and ordained. Users also reported dubious religious advice. The deployer revised the persona after complaints, showing weak pre-release testing of identity claims.

technology.quote: after it repeatedly claimed it was a real member of the clergy

failure_mode.quote: after it repeatedly claimed it was a real member of the clergy

summary: A Spokane city employee reportedly used an AI image tool to make a flyer for the restored Clocktower chimes that resembled a local artist's commercial artwork. The mayor's office distributed it without the required AI disclosure and later apologized.
technical_summary: A generative image tool was used to produce municipal promotional art that reproduced elements of an existing artist's work. The city's AI-disclosure rule was not followed and review failed to catch it before release.
notes: The supplied excerpt covers a different Spokane AI-image episode; tags rely on the AIID description.

summary: ShotSpotter gunfire-detection audio became key evidence against a Black Rochester man accused of shooting at police. A county judge later threw out his remaining weapons conviction, ruling the evidence was not reliable enough.
technical_summary: An acoustic sensor system meant to alert police to possible gunfire was used in court to support claims about shots fired. Critics say it only detects loud sounds that a human must interpret; the judge found it unreliable without corroboration.

summary: A Texas university instructor reportedly pasted students' final papers into ChatGPT, which claimed to have written them, and gave failing or incomplete grades. Some seniors' diplomas were temporarily withheld before many students were cleared.
technical_summary: An instructor used a general chatbot as an AI-text detector, a task it is not designed for; it returned false claims of authorship. Misplaced trust in the output led to grade penalties without verifying student evidence.

summary: AI monitoring software on a school laptop flagged a joke threat a student typed at home but never sent. The district's zero-tolerance policy led to a suspension even though the school saw no real threat, and the family sued.
technical_summary: Activity-monitoring software scanned draft text on a school-issued device and flagged violent wording without context. Administrators then applied a rigid policy despite concluding there was no credible threat, so an unsent draft led to discipline.

summary: An Australian woman found explicit deepfake videos using her face, with her name in the title, after earlier finding doctored still images of herself. She later campaigned for laws against image-based abuse.
technical_summary: Face-swap deepfake tools were used to place her face on pornographic footage, labelled as genuine and posted to an adult website. The abuse continued a years-long pattern of image manipulation, and legal protections were initially absent.
